violated_contract: A request whose connection dies in transit (network switch, lost route, TCP timeout, damaged TLS record) is a transient failure: it is never reported as a crash, never surfaced as a permanent sync error, keeps the recording queued, and its retry runs on a socket opened on the current network. package:http delivers these as a bare ClientException carrying only the OS error text (dart:io rewraps the socket error as HttpException), so a classifier keyed on the SocketException type misses them; on iOS a Wi-Fi/cellular switch under a reused keep-alive socket arrives as "Can't assign requested address" (EADDRNOTAVAIL, errno 49) and was the top iOS Crashlytics issue (434 users in 8 days to 2026-10-29).
canonical_prevention: Classify transport failures by the shape the HTTP stack actually delivers (the bare ClientException OS messages, matched only on ClientException so file errors stay reportable), and drop pooled keep-alive sockets after a transport failure or a network change so retries never reuse a socket bound to a vanished address.
